newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end firmer on month-end fund buying.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end firmer on month-end fund buying.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip shares closed firmer on Monday as fund managers balanced their books at the end of the month, dealers and analysts said on Monday.
The key Composite Index spiked up within the last half-hour of trading to close 7.24 points, or 0.68 percent, higher at 1,077.30, after having traded nearly unchanged for most of the day.
"Maybank, United Engineers and Telekom are all up. It's just window-dressing for the month-end book closing of fund managers," said a vice president of dealing at a local brokerage house.
Maybank, United Engineers and Telekom together account for around 22 percent of the weightage of the Composite Index.
Market volume was thin with 190 million shares traded, valued at 1,653 million ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers 352 to 231.

Small-capitalised stocks led most of the day's activity, with Chase Perdana topping the most-active list. The stock gained 70 cents to 22.70 ringgit. Chase said on Friday it plans to diversify into stockbroking with the acquisition of a substantial stake in a Sabah-based brokerage house for 22 million ringgit.
The imminent handover of Hong Kong to China at midnight on Tuesday did not have any discernable impact on the local bourse, analysts and dealers said.

Financial services group Affin Holdings Bhd closed five cents higher at 6.00 ringgit. The company said on Monday it planned to set up a joint stockbroking venture with United Overseas Bank Ltd of Singapore.

The improvement in liquidity caused by overnight interbank rates falling to 5.5 percent "encouraged some buying in high yielding stocks," said Singapore-based brokers G.K. Goh in a daily stock report.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Finacial Futures Exchange the spot June contract closed 5.9 points higher at 1,075.6 with 280 lots traded. July gained 2.0 points to 1,070.0 with 386 lots traded, and September fell 3.5 points to 1,071.5.
